activities.caption: stack the six stages of the climb
activities.name: lpStageOrder

config.prompt: Smilkstein's natural learning process — rebuild the six stages:
items: Motivation — something makes you want it
Advanced practice that builds a foundation
Refinement — polish with feedback and challenge
Mastery — the thing is truly yours
config.why: The stages are not a curriculum but a description of what brains do anyway — and under all of them the brain is physically changing, which is why getting things wrong during practice is the reorganisation itself.

activities.caption: pair each clause with what it rules out
activities.name: lpClauseMatch

config.prompt: The definition works by exclusion — pair each clause with what it rules out:

pairs.right: a yawn, a mood, tonight's cramming — it evaporates
what the learner could already do
maturation — a toddler's walking is development
learning as observable behaviour shaped by association and consequence
learning as a change in knowledge and mental structures

config.why: Every method of teaching is an attempt to cause the change deliberately — which is why a course about teaching starts with a course about learning.

activities.caption: your first month — which demand is in play?
activities.name: lpAxesBranch

config.root: Your first month of teaching, four moments from the paragraph — for each, what is being demanded of you?

start.text: Monday: several of your students speak English as a second language and the textbook assumes otherwise. What does the moment demand?

choices.label: Diagnose the learner
choices.feedback: Diversity converts "teach the class" into "diagnose the learner" — a professional skill, not a personality trait.

choices.label: Buy a better textbook
choices.feedback: A tool swaps the problem sideways — the diagnosis of the learners in front of you is still yours to make.

choices.label: Teach to the middle
choices.feedback: The paragraph's point is that one "class" no longer exists — many languages, cultures, abilities and prior knowledges sit in the room.

div.text: Next moment: the department adopts a learning-management system, then an AI tutor appears. What changes — and what does not?

choices.label: Tools change what the teacher plans, monitors and delivers — not what learning requires
choices.feedback: Exactly: attention, encoding, retrieval and motivation are the unchanged requirements underneath the changing tools.

choices.label: The tool removes the need for any of it
choices.feedback: No tool delivers attention or retrieval for the learner — that is the trap the paragraph warns about.

tech.text: Last moment: the school publishes results tables and sets grade targets. What arrives with that scoreboard?

choices.label: Benefits and risks together — focus and equity of expectations, but narrowing of what counts as learning
choices.feedback: Accountability's scoreboards carry both, which is why the professional reads them with evidence rather than fear.

choices.label: Pure benefit — targets focus everyone
choices.feedback: Half right — and the risk is real: what gets measured can narrow what counts as learning.

end.text: All three moments end in the same place: decisions justified by evidence, not folklore.

config.why: The thread that ties the profession together is reflective practice — the loop of planning, acting, watching the result and revising — which turns the job's constant decision-making into a research-informed craft.

activities.anchor: plan, act, observe the result, revise
activities.caption: in-the-moment or after-the-fact? file the reflections
activities.name: lpReflectBuckets

config.prompt: Schön's two versions — file each reflection:

items.label: Noticing mid-lesson that the explanation is not landing and changing course
Redrafting tomorrow's opener after today's lesson
Dropping a failing demo and switching to questions on the spot
Re-ordering next week's unit once the test results are in

config.why: Both are trainable, and both separate the professional from the merely experienced — reflection is the loop that makes constant decision-making possible.

activities.caption: bet before the intervention — what does refusal earn?
activities.name: lpRefusalPredict

config.q: A seven-year-old will not write. Watch what follows the refusal — which pay-off is doing the reinforcing?
choices: Escape from the task — the refusal works
config.why: The child often escapes the task (negative reinforcement: the behaviour "works") and gets attention besides. The intervention redesigns the consequences: steps small enough to complete, immediate reinforcement of completion, and no escape for refusal.

activities.anchor: each panel names a different way learning dies
activities.caption: fill the pipeline's bottlenecks
activities.name: lpPipelineCloze

config.text: Attention is the %%0%% of the whole pipeline; working memory holds about %%1%% ± 2 familiar items and evaporates in %%2%% without rehearsal; survival requires %%3%% — chunking and connecting to what is known; and every successful %%4%% re-entrenches the memory.
config.hint: Gate, seven, seconds, encoding, retrieval — five panels, five fates.

activities.caption: call the magnitude — the month-out curve
activities.name: lpEbbingEstimate

config.prompt: Ebbinghaus re-tested his nonsense syllables a full month after learning them. Roughly what share survived?
config.why: About 21% — the fall is front-loaded, with most of the loss inside the first day.
config.context: His slope is a warning, not a law of nature: nonsense syllables had no meaning, no schema and no review, so this curve is the floor, not the ceiling.

activities.anchor: The taxonomy gives teachers a vocabulary
activities.caption: pin the worked objective on Bloom's ladder
activities.name: lpBloomPlace

config.prompt: The worked objective — "predict what paving a floodplain does to runoff" — sits at which of Bloom's six levels?
config.why: Apply — using the concept in a new context. "List the stages of the water cycle" would be Remember; "explain why the cycle has no beginning" is Understand.
